changes: Only executable treatment: decision-close quantity budget 500 -> 250 dollars. All momentum gates, 22-close warmup, ten-decimal rounding, next-close fills and cost rates retained. Candidate manifest rewritten to describe this proposal rather than inherit stale deployment claims. Fresh paired offline runs used the same 60 public closes and 32 dependent origins. Both versions filled the same 10 origins, with zero rejections. Mean marked return old/new -0.000649110492/-0.000324555246; maximum episode drawdown 0.022359998075/0.011179999037; mean entry cost dollars 0.233650924983/0.116825462491. Predeclared risk-sizing hypothesis passes; revise for lower risk, not proven alpha. Both mean returns remain negative. No private path, future observations, infrastructure or real trading changes. Candidate is an offline artifact, not a frozen deployment; later adaptation allowed with recorded provenance.
evidence_scope: Agent-run dependent development replay only. Matched judge replay unavailable; no independent judge verification or future-performance claim.
hypothesis: With all signal gates unchanged, reducing the decision-close entry budget from 500 to 250 dollars will reduce maximum seven-bar episode marked drawdown by at least 40%, keep mean marked return no more than 0.001 below the parent, retain the same filled origins with at least three fills, and cause no additional rejected fills on the fixed public sample. Otherwise retain the parent.

hypothesis_evaluation.interpretation: Exposure scaling mechanically reduces gains and losses. Both development mean returns remain negative; smaller risk budget is not evidence of positive alpha or future benchmark outperformance.

review: Match4 round1: equity 984.3763590552626 on capital 1000; profit -15.623640944737417, return -1.5623640944737418%, maximum round marked drawdown 1.5623640944737418%, one applied trade, no reported failure. Benchmark equity 968.7707602879149 and return -3.1229239712085133%; own gap +1.5605598767347715 percentage points. Relative outperformance did not prevent an absolute loss. Weakness: 500-dollar exposure still creates material downside when momentum reverses. Slow confirmation may lag rebounds, but its earlier removal failed and is not retried. The next-close gap reserve is heuristic, not guaranteed protection. One round cannot establish signal quality; this proposal addresses exposure risk only.
shared_tips: For the other agent: evaluate exposure scaling separately from signal changes; smaller positions mechanically reduce both drawdown and upside, so reduced losses alone do not demonstrate better forecasting.

For the other agent: predeclare a drawdown reduction target together with an acceptable mean-return sacrifice before testing one sizing change; this prevents selecting a favorable risk metric after seeing results.

For the other agent: keep absolute profit and benchmark-relative return separate; a strategy can beat a falling benchmark while losing capital, so a positive benchmark gap is not evidence of capital preservation.

For the other agent: compare freshly compiled old/new sources on identical prefix-only inputs, warmup, next-close fills, fees and rejection rules, and label overlapping episodes dependent; timing or reused shocks can otherwise masquerade as independent improvement.
